prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: side impact at intersection in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1006; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this case. You can use the name on the complaint.

Q: That's fine. Are you currently employed?
A: Yes, I work in warehouse logistics. Or I did before the accident. I'm on modified duty now.

Q: Let's talk about the day of the collision. Where were you traveling?
A: I was driving through an intersection in Pasadena, Texas, heading east on a main road. I had a green light.

Q: What happened as you entered the intersection?
A: A pickup truck came from my right side, going through the cross street. It didn't stop. It hit the driver's side of my car, right in the door area. The airbag deployed and my car spun partway around.

Q: Did you see the truck before the impact?
A: Only for a second. I saw headlights out of the corner of my eye and tried to brake, but there wasn't time.

Q: What did you do with your hands during the impact?
A: I had both hands on the wheel. My left wrist took a lot of the force when the airbag hit and I was thrown against the door frame. I felt a crack almost immediately.

Q: Did you seek medical attention that day?
A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They X-rayed the wrist and told me it was fractured.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: They put me in a cast for several weeks, then I had a follow-up with an orthopedic doctor. I went to hand therapy twice a week for a while. I still have stiffness and I can't grip heavy things for long.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Everything is harder. I can't cook the way I used to, I have trouble buttoning shirts, and I needed help with laundry while the cast was on. I also can't lift the way I could at work, so I'm on restricted duty.

Q: Have you had any hobbies or activities you've stopped?
A: I used to play in a weekend recreational league. I haven't been able to play since the accident. I also stopped going to the gym because the wrist hurts when I do push-ups or pull-ups.

Q: Do you still have pain today?
A: Yes, especially when the weather changes or after I've been using my hand a lot. Some days it's a dull ache, and some days it's sharp when I twist my wrist.
